_note: Hand-maintained project data: stage status and risks. Each 'completed' stage must name its evidence (files in this repository). Update when a stage changes; the dashboard is rebuilt from this file plus generated evidence.

stages.name: Existing BR13A dashboard brought under version control and described in the bridge format
stages.plain: The working prototype (one HTML app) and BR13A's data are in GitHub, rebuildable byte-for-byte.

stages.name: Architecture, rules and verification plan
stages.plain: Agreed target design, working rules and how results will be checked.

stages.name: BR13A baseline (regression reference)
stages.plain: A recorded fingerprint of what today's software produces for BR13A, so any later change is noticed.
stages.review: audit report written; awaiting owner review

stages.name: Bridge data format 0.2 (keep original drawing values, overrides, file fingerprint)
stages.plain: Every change to a drawing value keeps the original and who approved the change.

stages.name: Standards data framework
stages.plain: All code-standard numbers in one reviewed place, each marked unverified until checked.
stages.review: awaiting owner review; content NOT approved

stages.name: Geometry generation (Python)
stages.plain: Bridge geometry computed from the bridge data alone, for any bridge.

stages.name: Sections and products
stages.plain: Girder and deck properties from one Super-T definition.

stages.name: Structural model builder and analysis core
stages.plain: Build the analysis model from the bridge data instead of a fixed BR13A file.

stages.name: Independent structural verification
stages.plain: Check results against an independent MIDAS model and textbook cases.

stages.name: PDF extraction and decision workflow
stages.plain: Read the drawings into the bridge data; engineer approves decisions in the app.
stages.note: an earlier extraction prototype exists but is not connected

stages.name: Second-bridge validation
stages.plain: Run a different bridge end to end with no code changes.

next.task: P1 geometry engine in Python (from the bridge description, MGA, straight chords)
next.why: Geometry is the first engine layer; every later stage (sections, model, analysis) builds on it, and it must work for any bridge, not only BR13A.
next.evidence: 4 synthetic validation cases to 1 mm with hand-checked coordinates; BR13A girder chords equal the baseline to 1 mm; no BR13A constants in code

risks.title: Girder end region over-utilised in the current design run
risks.plain: Near the bearings (x = 0.75 m) bending and shear/torsion utilisation exceed 1.0. The end zone (solid end block) is not defined, and strands are placeholders.
risks.why: Could be a real design issue or a missing input; it must be resolved before any girder design is relied on.

risks.title: No result is independently verified yet
risks.plain: All numbers are reproducible outputs of the current software. None has been checked against an independent model.
risks.why: Software tests passing does not mean the bridge results are right.

risks.title: 177 assumed input values in BR13A
risks.plain: Placeholders let the model run; each needs data or an engineer decision.

risks.title: Strand and bar layout are placeholders
risks.plain: A standard T4 layout is used because the BR13A strand drawings are not in the set.
risks.why: Design capacities and stresses depend on them.

risks.title: Design engine neutral axis differs from the worked example
risks.plain: Capacity matches but the neutral-axis depth is about 8 % off.
risks.why: Indicates an engine difference that may matter in other cases.

risks.title: Code-standard values not yet verified
risks.plain: 63 code-standard values are now inventoried in one place (standards/REVIEW_REGISTER.md), but none is verified against an authorised copy; 27 need specialist interpretation.
risks.why: Every design action depends on them.

risks.title: Analysis model is a fixed BR13A file
risks.plain: The model is not yet generated from bridge data.
risks.why: Blocks use on any other bridge.

risks.title: Simplified load combination envelopes
risks.plain: Traffic moment, shear and torsion are enveloped separately; earthquake results are unsigned.
risks.why: Can be conservative or, for some checks, not concurrent.

risks.title: Some plots draw invalid coordinates
risks.plain: 88 drawing errors per run (no calculation error).
risks.why: A plot may show wrong or missing lines.
